content.statement: Where State action restricts Fundamental Rights, courts may examine whether the restriction is proportionate to the legitimate aim — including suitability, necessity, and balance — as developed in Indian privacy and related jurisprudence. Apply only as supported by controlling authority for the right and context engaged.
elements: Necessity (least restrictive means where required by doctrine)
content.development: Prominent in modern Article 21 privacy and related Fundamental Rights review; verify the governing tests for the specific right before pleading.
content.application: Use in challenges to invasive restrictions on liberty, privacy, and analogous interests where authority supports proportionality analysis.
exceptions: Not a freestanding substitute for the text of Articles 14, 19 and 21
